en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Jar.
4. The Question on the Factors of a Field “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘three factors of a field should be adopted,’ which are those three factors that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a field is endowed with good irrigation channels;”
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga must be one who has fulfilled the preliminary duties and the code of proper conduct.
This, Great King, is the first factor of a field that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, a field is well-defined by its boundaries, and by means of those boundaries, water is protected so that the grain may ripen.

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga must be endowed with virtue, moral shame, and propriety. Having protected the state of a recluse through that virtue, moral shame, and propriety, he should attain the four fruits of recluseship.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the field that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, a field is productive; it brings joy to the farmer, for even a small seed sown becomes much, and what is sown in abundance becomes even more abundant.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the spiritual life, must be endowed with exertion and be one who yields abundant fruit;
he must be one who brings joy to the donors, such that what is given in small measure becomes much, and what is given in great measure becomes even greater.
This, Great King, is the third quality of a field that should be adopted.
This was also said, Great King, by the Elder Upāli, the master of the Vinaya:
"This is indeed called the best field,
Thus ends the fourth inquiry, on the factors of the field.
